title: Leech/Turyn research (no κ claim): scoped fitting bounds and cost screens
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR records exact Leech/Turyn constructions, tested transformations, and scoped obstructions to smaller binary fitting dimensions. It preserves the failed directions as reproducible research and identifies the freedom that remains open. No production supplier or selected exponent certificate changes.

### Results and scope

| Result | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|
| A Turyn product kernel with 23,040 ports, real rank 512, and a valid 27-bit fitting representation | Exact generation and all 530,841,600 ordered pair checks. Within each fixed profile, a dyadic change of basis reduces the kernel to 64 E8 copies. Sharing the real centers across profiles remains relevant. |
| Glue-class-constant fitting dimension is exactly 27 | Nine 24-cliques with even vertex incidences give a characteristic-two rank bound, including normalized block fits. This does **not** assume those quotient cliques lift simultaneously to individual ports. |
| Each individual full profile needs symmetric binary dimension nine | A 24-port witness is exhausted without a SAT solver in 43 search nodes; cyclic copies cover all three profiles. This alone does not add to a global 27-dimensional bound. |
| Several full-port transformations cannot reduce the dimension | Four actual edges obstruct independent source/target block-sign choices. Exact finite constraints rule out an improvement from affine Leech coordinates and the tested 168-feature nonlinear family. The latter permits separate affine glue maps for all eight high-line positions and quadratic glue terms. |
| Real basis changes alone cannot reduce the existing full-port encoder bill | Every nonzero real linear tensor encoder has support rank 27 under the existing labels; rank-minimal 512-feature factorizations therefore cost at least 13,824. Redundant encoders outside the tensor column space are excluded from this bound. |
| Full Leech-shell alternatives and scoped moment budgets | The 98,280-line cubic kernel has a 2,600-center dyadic factorization. Norm-six directions reduce the tested encoder support rank to 24, but their dyadic decoder and complete word remain unbuilt. Cost relaxations are explicitly separated from constructed suppliers. |

The hosting-aware accounting relaxation gives nominal κ ≈ 0.00142611820 for the full 27-bit Turyn recipe, about 11.6% below the **reported** PR592 frontier. The punctured recipe has about 1.06% optimistic headroom before the omitted construction obligations. These are bounds within stated scheduling and center-cost assumptions, **not universal limits on dimension 27**. Neither PR592's supplier nor PR595's complete structural analysis is freshly replayed here.

### Packages and reproduction

The branch starts from `main` at `7dfa22b` and adds only:

- `research/leech-lattice/`: geometry, transformations, factorizations, support calculations, and initial screens.
- `research/turyn-code-space/`: the exact glue-quotient rank obstruction and affine/quadratic search spaces.
- `research/turyn-port-labels/`: full-port finite certificates, encoder-support bound, and updated scoped costs.

Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10, NumPy, and a C++17 compiler for the complete code-space replay. No SAT solver is required. Each package pins its files and inherited inputs.

```sh
python3 -I -O research/leech-lattice/verify.py --output /tmp/leech-replay
python3 -I -O research/turyn-code-space/verify.py --output /tmp/turyn-code-replay
python3 -I -O research/turyn-port-labels/verify.py --output /tmp/turyn-port-replay
```

All three packages have passed their exact replay, including optimized Python checks. The frozen first two packages retain their corruption controls; the full-port package includes the known nine-bit fit and a relaxed eight-bit fitting control. No GitHub CI result or formal code review is claimed.

### What remains open

An arbitrary global 25-dimensional full-port fit is still open. The finite family obstructions do not exclude richer nonlinear labels, other scalar kernels, redundant factorizations, or different paid controllers. Even a compatible labeling would still need a charged scalar circuit, frame moves, helper clearing and hosting, and the inherited outer checks. Nothing here establishes worst-case O(1) indexing or an improved multiplication exponent.
